title: Pet-Friendly Hotels in Chattanooga, Tennessee | PetTripFinder
meta_description: Verified pet-friendly hotels across Greater Chattanooga, Tennessee, with real pet fees and policies read from each hotel's own official website.
introductory_copy: Every listing links to a pet policy verified directly from the hotel's own official website.
_boundary_note: PTF-CHATTANOOGA-TN-NEW-MARKET-001 visitor market: the Greater Chattanooga practical traveler lodging market, which is Hamilton County, Tennessee. The market is defined by municipality and county geography and by real lodging concentration on I-24, I-75 and US-27, not by the marketing reach of the destination bureau, which promotes a multi-state region reaching Cleveland and Kimball in Tennessee and Ringgold, Fort Oglethorpe, Chickamauga and McLemore in Georgia.
_tennessee_georgia_border_rule: PTF-CHATTANOOGA-TN-NEW-MARKET-001 Phase 6, BINDING. This market admits TENNESSEE municipalities only. The Tennessee/Georgia line runs about four miles south of the East Ridge lodging cluster, and the Battlefield Parkway corridor in Fort Oglethorpe and the I-75 exits 348 to 350 cluster in Ringgold, Catoosa County, Georgia, market themselves as Chattanooga lodging. Prose is not geography. A property whose OWN page states a Georgia address is classified NORTH_GEORGIA_FRINGE_HOLD and is held outside the promoted set, whatever its name says. The hold is a founder decision, not a silent exclusion: the rows and their evidence are carried in the founder packet so a later order can admit a named Georgia cluster deliberately, through explicit_hotel_ids on a corridor created for it, and never by widening a postal partition.
_corridor_note: Corridors are a postal-code partition (census_membership_basis CORRIDOR_REGISTRY). Every Hamilton County, Tennessee postal code that carries traveler lodging belongs to exactly one corridor; no postal code appears twice. A legitimate fringe property that the partition cannot reach is admitted by explicit_hotel_ids on the corridor that actually serves its travelers, never by widening a postal code to capture one hotel.
